name: Christmas cake
origin: The British rich fruit cake traditionally made weeks or months ahead of Christmas and fed with spirits as it matures, then finished with marzipan and royal icing; a descendant of medieval plum porridge via the 16th-century plum cake.

ingredients.note: an even higher fruit load than Dundee cake, real for the richest British Christmas cake formulas; see dundee-cake.json for the same conservative treatment of dried fruit's own moisture
a measure of brandy mixed directly into the batter itself, distinct from the further feeding of spirits into the baked cake as it matures (which is a post-bake soak, out of scope here)

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat butter and sugar until light

process.name: fold in flour, spice and fruit
process.description: fold in flour, leavening, salt and mixed spice, then the dried fruit and candied peel

process.name: bake
process.description: bake very low and slow, protecting the top from over-browning

notes: Even richer in dried fruit than Dundee cake, matching the real reputation of a British Christmas cake as the densest, most fruit-heavy of the family; the very low, long bake is standard practice, documented across British home-baking references, to cook such a dense mass through without over-browning the outside. Marzipan and royal icing are applied weeks later, well after baking, and are out of scope for this batter's formulation.
